text:
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from current intent. MSMT-LSI (2024) uses separate long/short attention networks with multiple temporal embeddings; [hierarchical preference modeling (online 2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) adds dynamically routed long-term interest vectors, selects those matching short-term intent, and fuses them with time encoding. [DSRec (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) is especially relevant: historical aggregation for stable interests, a local-intent branch whose state evolution depends on time gaps, and residual cross-fusion between branches. These mechanisms motivate adaptive alternatives to a fixed five-item residual, but do not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

Separate branches alone do not establish disentanglement. [CLSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13090) supplies an earlier practical template: history-derived long/short interest proxies, contrastive supervision, adaptive aggregation, and counterfactual evaluation. For SASRec, a lightweight experimental inference is to combine the existing representation with several causal decay pools and a learned gate conditioned on observed history and elapsed gaps. Interest states remain latent hypotheses; histories cannot establish users’ conformity or diversity traits.

Controlled comparisons matter: [Spotify’s October 2026 study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) reports pairwise-transition models beating both Transformer reproductions on four of five benchmarks. Proposed ablations: fixed versus learned mixing, one versus multiple timescales, and real versus constant/shuffled gaps while holding item order and positions fixed. For deletion probes, compare preserving original position indices against compacting the sequence. Select using the common macro validation HR@10; these controls test predictive contributions without claiming causal recency effects.
